If the nation were fighting for its life, is it ever acceptable for the government to take steps to block certain ideas from forming within a society? For example, taking an alternative scenario to WWII. The year is 1965. London, and Moscow have fallen to the Third Reich. Greenland is the last US stronghold guarding the Atlantic seaboard. If it falls, the US will be doomed. The anti-war movement gains momentum. Would the government be in the right to take steps to "disappear" key figures supporting the anti-war efforts, or even stage false flags to make the movement look bad? Perhaps they use the media, and schools to ensure public support in pushing back the Nazis.

Where is the line drawn with government censorship? I believe an extreme of either side is wrong. In my opinion the survival of any nation depends upon the government dispersing thoughts which aid, and abet the nation's enemy. e.g. Taking care of people who spread ISIS propaganda to youth.

Obviously no government is perfect, and power can always be misused for personal gain. What are your thoughts?
